title: Tenant-aware retention SLA, ingest backpressure, and index compaction plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Audit ingest volume varies heavily between tenants (spikes from heavy platform customers and pen tests). Current storage retention is a flat policy that leads to ballooning costs and poor query performance for smaller tenants. We need a tenant-aware retention enforcement mechanism, ingest backpressure to preserve SLOs under load, and a safe index compaction/merge schedule that reduces storage while preserving query fidelity for compliance queries.
goals: Implement tenant-level retention SLAs that can be configured per-account (e.g., 7d/30d/90d) with automatic enforcement
Add ingest-layer backpressure and rate-limiting that gates non-critical audit traffic when global index throughput threatens latency SLOs
Introduce an index compaction pipeline (merge + dedupe) and cold-store spill policy to reclaim storage and lower query costs
Provide observability: per-tenant storage delta, compaction savings, and SLO breach alerts
proposed_solution_summary: 1) Add retention metadata to tenant profiles and enforce via a retention-enforcer service that marks shards/segments for TTL and eviction. 2) Integrate an ingest-side token bucket throttler tied to per-tenant budgets and global headroom signals from the indexer. 3) Implement scheduled compaction jobs per partition that run aggressively on hot partitions with high duplication, and off-peak compaction for cold partitions, coupled with coldstore spill of blobs older than X days. 4) Expose controls in Console for setting tenant SLAs and visualizing projected cost impact.
tradeoffs: Tighter per-tenant retention reduces storage costs but increases risk of missing events for long-tail forensic queries
Ingest throttling protects global SLOs but may delay audit events (mitigated by burst windows and priority classes)
Aggressive compaction reduces cost but increases CPU/GPU IO during compaction windows—need to schedule during low-traffic windows and provide throttling
Complexity added to billing and Console UX to surface per-tenant retention and projected savings
architecture_notes: Retention-Enforcer service will subscribe to partition metadata and lease segments for eviction; it writes tombstones to index coordinator to ensure consistent deletion across replicas
Ingest Throttler sits in front of the write path and consults the RatePolicy store (tenant config + global headroom). It emits backpressure metrics and counters per tenant.
Compaction orchestrator will be a cron-driven job with concurrency limits and per-node compaction quotas; compaction will run vectorized dedupe + light-weight reindexing to maintain query correctness
Coldstore pipeline will blob older segments to object storage with compact manifest and restore path for ad-hoc forensic queries (restore cost estimate exposed in Console)
All actions must be auditable and recorded in the admin audit log (linking to RBAC v2 roles so only allowed admins can change retention or force compaction)
Integrations: SSO/SAML for Console grants; changes emit policy-change audit events
metrics_and_slos: Ingest latency P95 under 200ms (tail during backpressure events allowed to spike to 500ms for non-critical writes)
Index write throughput target 50k events/s per index cluster before backpressure engages
Retention enforcement correctness: 100% of segments older than configured TTL are marked for eviction within 24 hours of expiry
Compaction CPU budget: <= 15% of node CPU over rolling 1h average during business hours
Cost target: reduce cold storage bill for audit by 30% for customers with 90d policy in the first 90 days
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Implement retention metadata and enforcement in staging and run for internal tenants only (1 week)
Phase 1: Enable ingest throttler in read-only monitoring mode (emit metrics but do not drop) for 2 weeks
Phase 2: Gradually enable throttling for <5% of tenants (low-impact accounts) with fail-open policy; run compaction in test cluster
Phase 3: Open Console controls to operations and selected customers; enable tenant SLA config for self-serve customers in beta
Phase 4: Full rollout with SLO alerts and automatic cost dashboards
security_considerations: Retention and compaction settings are sensitive — only admins with 'audit:manage_retention' role (RBAC v2) can modify
All retention changes are logged to immutable audit ledger with SAML identity mapped to user email
Coldstore restore requires approval workflow for eDiscovery and will record a chain-of-custody in the audit log
Ensure tombstone propagation cannot be abused by compromised service accounts: enforce signed requests and rotate keys
acceptance_criteria: Retention metadata stored per-tenant and UI control created in Console (QA-tested)
Ingest throttler metrics show correct per-tenant budgets and global headroom signals (monitored in staging)
Compaction jobs run on schedule and show measurable storage reclaimed in the test cluster (>15% for candidate partitions)
Integration test proving tombstone propagation and successful eviction in a 3-replica cluster
RBAC gating: only users with audit:manage_retention can edit retention; changes visible in audit log

2025-02-03 - QA: Failed test case - tombstone propagation out of order on partition boundary. Root cause: race between retention-enforcer and partition rollover. Working on fix (ENG-82498).
2025-02-10 - PM (Ruth Novak): Prioritize expose of projected cost-savings in Console before general availability. Minor UI follow-up added to scope.
